summary: Employee reimbursement amounts routed to duplicate ledger codes after payroll sync
description:
Issue summary:
Several employee reimbursement payments processed on 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10 were posted to the wrong GL ledger code and, in several cases, resulted in duplicate ledger entries. Impacted reimbursements are visible in the February-March accrual reconciliation.

Impact:
- 9 reimbursement transactions (total $4,130.75) posted to duplicate ledger codes, causing mismatch in the AP aging and GL.
- Payroll runs for March show an unexpected debit/credit variance on the expense bucket.
- Finance cannot close the March payroll accrual until entries are corrected; potential delay to month-end close.

Environment:
- Production finance system: NetLedger v3.4 (hosted), payroll-sync lambda (aws us-east-1), reconciliation job FIN-ACC-RUN-01.

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Reimbursement submitted by employee via Expensify on 2026-03-02 (reimbursement IDs in attachments).
2) Expense approved and exported to finance queue on 2026-03-03.
3) Payroll-sync job executed on 2026-03-09 (incremental sync) and again on 2026-03-10 (retry).
4) After sync, 9 reimbursements appear twice: once under ledger 5600-TRAVEL and once under 5600-TRAVEL-01 (an older/deprecated subsidiary code).
5) Audit trail shows the second posting was created by payroll-sync lambda triggered by a reprocess attempt; origin user is service-account:fin-sync.

Expected behavior:
- Single posting to the active ledger code for the subsidiary linked to the employee cost center.
- Reprocessing should not duplicate already-posted reimbursements (idempotency).

Additional context:
- A recent change (PR 2345) introduced a mapping override to support a merged subsidiary mapping; mapping table contains both "5600-TRAVEL" and legacy "5600-TRAVEL-01" entries.
- Similar-sounding ticket INT-32714 (contractor reimbursement normalization) referenced for historical mapping approaches.
- Priority: needs correction before month-end close (EOD 2026-03-15).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Evelyn Ross: Filed after discovering GL mismatch during accrual reconciliation. Attached example CSV with affected IDs.
2026-03-10 - Nina Kapoor: Acknowledged. Triage started. Tagging payments-engineering and payroll-infra. Will pull logs and check reprocess rules.

2026-03-11 - Marco Reyes (payments-engineering): Initial review: payroll-sync lambda returned HTTP 200 on both runs; NetLedger accepted both POSTs because transaction GUID differed on reprocess. Suspect idempotency key missing on retry path.

2026-03-11 - Li Chen (payroll-infra): Confirmed mapping table contains duplicate mapping rows for legacy and merged codes. PR 2345 added mapping override but did not include idempotency header. Reproduced duplicate post locally by re-running sync script with same expense UUID but updated mapping resolution order.

2026-03-12 - Nina Kapoor: Temporary mitigation applied: disabled auto-reprocess for expenses older than 7 days. Finance applied manual reversing entries for 6 of the 9 duplicates to unblock close; 3 remain pending vendor/employee confirmation.
2026-03-13 - Evelyn Ross: Confirmed manual reversals applied for 6 items; two employees acknowledged and one disputed (partial amount). Scheduling follow-up with HR.
investigation_notes: Checked payroll-sync logs: two distinct runs (run_id 20260309-12 and run_id 20260310-03) both processed same expense UUIDs after mapping change.
NetLedger API requires an idempotency-key header; payroll-sync only sets idempotency-key when origin_event_id is present. Reprocess path omitted origin_event_id.
Mapping resolution now performs 'best match' fallback and returns legacy code for employees with ambiguous cost_center strings.
Local repro: re-run of sync script with mapping order change produced duplicate postings to 5600-TRAVEL and 5600-TRAVEL-01.
Scope: 9 transactions across 3 employees; no evidence of mass duplication beyond these due to targeted reprocess activity.
Related artifacts: reproduced in staging; test coverage for idempotency header missing in finance-integration tests.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to patch payroll-sync to always include idempotency-key derived from expense UUID on any NetLedger POST (PR ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/finance-integrations/pull/2345).
2) Add a one-time reconciliation job to detect duplicate postings by expense UUID and create undo entries for confirmed duplicates (run by Finance ops after approval).
3) Update mapping table to remove legacy code fallback or mark legacy rows as archived; coordinate with Finance to confirm mapping changes.
4) Add unit/integration tests to ensure idempotency behavior is enforced for reprocess paths.
5) Communicate to affected employees and HR for the disputed item; finalize manual correction by 2026-03-14 EOD.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation applied: auto-reprocess toggled off and 6 duplicates manually reversed to allow month-end close (finance journal IDs in attachments).
Engineering has a patch in PR 2345 to set idempotency-key; awaiting code review and QA in staging (target deploy 2026-03-15).
Reconciliation job spec drafted and posted to Confluence; Finance ops to run after deploy and give sign-off.
Post-deploy action: run duplicate-detection and apply reversal for the remaining 3 records pending employee confirmation.
Follow-up: add monitoring alert if duplicate postings exceed threshold (currently proposed threshold = 3 duplicates/24h).
